series.name: Development Methodologies
series.description: Determines workflow cadence, quality practices, and collaboration patterns aligned with procedural scope and tech constraints.

open_ended.text: What development process or methodology best fits this project? How should work be planned and tracked?

follow_up_choices.text: Sprint-based agile (Scrum) — fixed-length iterations with formal ceremonies
Continuous flow (Kanban) — pull-based with WIP limits, no fixed iterations

open_ended.text: What is the expected team size, composition, and structure?

follow_up_choices.text: Solo or pair — 1–2 people, all roles combined
Small team — 3–6 people with distinct roles (dev, design, PM)
Multiple teams — 7+ people across 2+ squads with coordination overhead

open_ended.text: What code review, testing, and quality assurance practices should be followed?

follow_up_choices.text: Light — ad-hoc reviews, manual testing, minimal automation
Standard — mandatory reviews, unit + integration tests, CI gates
Rigorous — pair programming, TDD, property-based testing, full automation

open_ended.text: How should the team handle technical debt, refactoring, and code quality?

follow_up_choices.text: Opportunistic — clean as you go, no formal tracking
Budgeted — allocate X% of each sprint to debt reduction
Formal — tracked backlog with dedicated quality improvement cycles

open_ended.text: How should the team communicate, share knowledge, and manage decisions?

follow_up_choices.text: Async-first — written docs, Slack/Teams, minimal meetings
Balanced — regular standups, weekly syncs, supplemented by async
Sync-heavy — daily standups, frequent pairing, co-located or synchronous remote

open_ended.text: What is the decision-making and escalation process? How are architectural choices made?

follow_up_choices.text: BDFL — one person makes final decisions with input
Consensus-driven — team agrees, with escalation to lead if deadlocked
ADR-based — proposals, reviews, and recorded Architecture Decision Records
